scope.description: Bounded, deterministic measurement of whether a deliberately dropped follower Accepted reply is repaired within 100 resend periods while no client proposal is made, and which protocol messages carry the repair if it happens.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt
error-free memory storage; everything except the one Accepted is delivered, in order, with no crash
one logical step per node equals one tick(); the 500-step window covers 100 configured resend periods
excluded: claims about which repair path is reachable in a deployment

basis.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently and never in real time. One logical step = tick(pid1), take_outgoing_messages(pid1), deliver them, then the same for pid2, so BLE replies are delivered within the round that requested them. Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, deliberately discard exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt) while delivering everything else, then run 500 steps = 100 configured resend periods with no further client proposal. It emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,after_drop,accept_decide_total,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts only that the trigger happened (exactly one Accepted dropped), that the follower really holds the entry as Undecided with accepted_idx 1, and that exactly one AcceptDecide exists in the whole run; whether the leader decided inside the window is the measured operand. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and it is read only after 20 extra steps so the Decide can reach the follower (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides).

before.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

prefix.before: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.

revision_reason: Same cluster and window, two corrections. (1) Cadence fidelity: the previous harness ticked both nodes and only then drained and delivered, which can leave a heartbeat reply arriving in a later BLE round than the request that asked for it and can provoke leadership churn; the fixed cadence ticks one node, drains and delivers it, then does the same for the other, so replies land in the round that asked. (2) The probe no longer predicts the outcome: it asserts the environment (exactly one AcceptDecide in the whole run, i.e. no new client proposal) and traces what the protocol itself puts on the wire after the deliberate drop (after_drop), so the receipt names the repair path if one exists. The control now runs 20 further steps after the leader decides before reading the follower's decided index (the previous attempt read it while the Decide was still in flight, which made the control fail for a harness reason).
